paper.title_en: Event-by-event identified particle net-charge fluctuations using the D measure in Au+Au collisions at FAIR energies
paper.abstract_en: Event-by-event fluctuations of conserved quantities provide sensitive information on the microscopic dynamics of strongly interacting matter created in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. In this work, we investigate the fluctuation measure D for net-charge, net-pion, net-kaon, and net-proton multiplicities in central Au+Au collisions at FAIR energies within the hadron-string dynamics (HSD) and parton-hadron-string dynamics (PHSD) transport approaches. The study covers beam energies $E_{\textrm{lab}} = 4A$-12A GeV in the SIS100 range, together with 15A and 25A GeV. The dependence of the fluctuation strength on the pseudorapidity window $\Delta \eta $ is analyzed for each particle species. For all observables, the D measure decreases with increasing $\Delta \eta $, indicating a strong acceptance dependence. Over the FAIR energy range considered here, the beam-energy dependence remains comparatively weak, whereas the particle-species dependence is pronounced. Among the observables studied, net-kaon fluctuations exhibit a pronounced HSD-PHSD separation, indicating an enhanced sensitivity to strangeness-related dynamics; however, the magnitude of the separation is energy- and acceptance-dependent. The present results provide a transport-model baseline for future measurements of identified-particle fluctuations at FAIR.
